key_findings: One index patient: a 67-year-old man with a right ventricle and pulmonary artery mass. He had emergency resection with VSD patch closure and tricuspid valve replacement. Pathology showed poorly differentiated metastatic adenocarcinoma with partial neuroendocrine differentiation. He had a cardiopulmonary arrest and died on postoperative day 3.

Tumor origin is hedged ("probably originated from the lungs"; later "lungs, gastrointestinal tract or pancreaticobiliary system"), and the family declined autopsy. primary_site stays null, and the origin is kept as an ambiguity.

In the admission paragraph, only the first sentence carries "On admission"; the other findings have no time of their own and are grouped under the admission event. The laboratory tests have no stated time.

Units are kept as printed (sodium and potassium in mg/dl; total bilirubin 8.4 g/dl with range 6.6-8.3), with an ambiguity. high flags are set only where the source says elevated or lengthened, or names leukocytosis. Glucose, urea and creatinine have no flag.

Thrombus is recorded as possible/provisional: the CT "interpreted to represent a thrombus", surgery later "found that the mass was a tumor", and the source never states that thrombus was excluded. Mitral valve replacement "not considered" is recorded as absent with action unknown. Paracetamol for years and the recent unspecified medication have action unknown and are not linked to each other.

All four figures were viewed at full resolution with upscaled crops. The CT coronal image has a burned-in ID-like numeric string and header text in the upper corners (direct_identifiers is correct). The echo panels carry only device or preset text.
residual_risks: The "history of pulmonary embolism" phrase may be a wording artefact for the suspected pulmonary embolism. Both readings are kept review_only.
Total bilirubin 8.4 g/dl with range 6.6-8.3 looks like a mislabelled analyte (possibly total protein). It is kept literally as total bilirubin with an ambiguity.
The admission-to-work-up relations rest on the order-only stay ruling, not on explicit time words.
